correctness.rationale: A derivation is uniquely its ordinary multiplication-by-h part, with h=alpha(h)+beta(h), plus an ordinary group-ring derivation commuting with alpha and beta. The truncated-log coordinates diagonalize these constraints; every allowed basis element satisfies Leibniz, and the complete bracket table follows from standard operator commutators. Direct modular elimination for all scalars at p=3,5,7,11 and direct generator/bracket checks substantiate, but are not the general proof.

originality.rationale: The conclusion classifies all derivations and their Lie brackets for every non-dihedral scalar prime Alexander quandle in defining characteristic. The 2021 primary paper treats characteristic-zero dihedral and isolated modular examples, and the 2026 primary paper supplies group-ring transport but does not classify derivations. Earlier defining-characteristic dihedral classifications are excluded, and earlier nonmodular derivation classifications assume a different field characteristic. Exact implication comparisons identified no coverage of the non-dihedral uniform formula, with residual historical-priority uncertainty.
